title: Simplify multilingual platform installation examples
outOfScope: Changing Runtime, installer, calibration-session schema, or repository governance behavior.
Removing the documented evidence, Unknown, human-approval, release-verification, or lifecycle boundaries.
Changing installation homepage, calibration guide, troubleshooting guide, or immutable historical Work Item evidence except through existing links from the platform pages.

sources.reason: Defines Work Item as the approved calibration route after Runtime installation.
Provides the existing symptom-first recovery route that platform entry pages must link rather than duplicate.
Current checker still requires obsolete platform-stage tables and must instead enforce the short multilingual Work Item route.
Records the previous prompt-first installation design whose platform surface must now be corrected without deleting the safety boundary.
Generates the Japanese source-bound assessment that must be refreshed after Japanese public documentation and focused documentation tests change.

riskAssessment.reason: Nine user-facing documents and their anti-omission checker must converge on the same short Work Item-first route without weakening safety boundaries.

executionDecision.reason: The user approved the short platform entry design and explicitly required complete English, Chinese, and Japanese coverage.

preReviewWarnings: Review every platform-language pair; no language may retain the old seven-stage table, filled-answer table, or cross-step navigation.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Each of the iOS, Android, and Java examples exists in English, Chinese, and Japanese and uses the same short entry structure: identify the platform, create a calibration Work Item, submit one short platform-aware prompt, and state a plain-language next action.

No platform entry page requires a first-time user to follow the obsolete seven-stage table, filled-answer table, cross-step navigation, Candidate/session internals, or lifecycle closure before creating the calibration Work Item.

Each platform entry preserves its material non-claim boundary and directs detailed calibration questions to the existing calibration guide and STOP recovery to the existing troubleshooting route rather than removing safety guidance.

The documentation checker and focused regression tests reject a missing platform-language entry, missing Work Item route, missing recovery/calibration route, missing evidence boundary, or legacy seven-stage structure.

The canonical pre-release documentation-alignment and Japanese source-bound assessment reports are refreshed and focused documentation checks pass; full local quality is optional under the user's temporary efficiency authorization while Hosted CI remains required.
guidelines: Keep first-time platform installation simple: the user sees where to start, what prompt to copy, and what happens next.
Use Work Item calibration as the single guided route; do not expose Session, Candidate, phase-record, or lifecycle internals on platform entry pages.
Preserve calibrated trust: Unknown is not guessed, safety boundaries are not weakened, and detailed recovery remains available by link.
Maintain complete English, Chinese, and Japanese semantic and structural coverage for all three platforms.

intent.problem: The installation homepages became beginner-oriented, but all nine iOS, Android, and Java platform examples remain the older 117–142-line seven-stage, multi-table process. They reintroduce governance terminology, cross-step navigation, and detailed lifecycle obligations before a novice can start calibration.
constraints: Do not omit English, Chinese, or Japanese variants for iOS, Android, or Java.
Keep the user-facing entry pages short and Work Item-first; retain detailed safety and recovery guidance through existing links.
Do not claim available toolchains, devices, signing, services, credentials, hosted CI, or project commands without repository evidence.
Use focused verification under the temporary user-authorized efficiency exception; do not waive governance gates or Hosted CI.
intent.rationale: Installation adoption depends on a non-programmer understanding the next action. Governance remains strong when Runtime and the calibration Work Item enforce evidence, while the entry documentation hides unnecessary internal mechanics.

rawUserRequest: 安装文档改善已经Okay，但是iOS,android,java的安装事例还是旧的复杂版本。请确认下。开个WI，修复。注意多语言不要遗漏。确认，请开始

declaredIntent.summary: Replace the obsolete complex multilingual platform installation examples with short Work Item-first entry pages, while preserving safety boundaries and enforcing all nine language-platform variants.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A first-time iOS, Android, or Java adopter in English, Chinese, or Japanese opens a platform page and can identify the platform, copy one short prompt, and create the calibration Work Item without navigating a seven-stage installation protocol.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Every one of the nine pages provides the same short Work Item-first route and a platform-specific non-claim boundary.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused documentation tests plus the metadata checker; mutate one required platform route in the regression test.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A platform fact such as toolchain, signing, service, device, command, or hosted CI is Unknown.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The entry page directs the reader to evidence-based calibration or STOP recovery and does not invent a platform fact.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Review every platform-language page for its explicit non-claim marker and calibration/troubleshooting links, then enforce them through the checker.

verification.reason: Temporary user-authorized focused-verification exception; it does not waive governance gates or Hosted CI.
